evidence: The assigned task and current plan require ml02-cart when regression trees are used. The current draft page and actual supplier bodies were inspected. def-empirical-decision-tree defines finite regression trees with nonempty leaf sample sets partitioning the training indices; alg-cart-greedy-split specifies a finite-depth regression-tree fit; thm-cart-greedy-split-is-best-listed-split-and-terminates proves a finite tree with nonempty children and bounded depth. This records actual interface verification, not acceptance of the draft suppliers.

The actual Definition states that leaf sample sets partition the finite sample and that every input follows a unique stored path. The gradient algorithm uses exactly these nonempty terminal sample sets and feature regions for its leafwise updates. The supplier is a draft; its body is read, with no approval claimed.

The actual Definition takes finite regression data, a finite maximum depth, uses midpoint candidate thresholds, and returns a tree with regression-mean leaves. The gradient algorithm fits this procedure to the pseudo-residual targets and uses the resulting regions; its later leaf offsets are separate exact loss minimizers. The supplier is a draft; its body is read, with no approval claimed.

The actual theorem proves that finite-depth CART returns a finite tree, with nonempty children at each split and depth at most the supplied cap. Step 3.1 gives the termination argument; the consumer needs the finite output and nonempty leaf partition. Its regression-loss clause uses the actual thm-node-mean-minimizes-squared-error supplier. The theorem and relevant supplier proof were inspected; this is not draft acceptance.

The actual Definition supplies a partition of the training indices by nonempty terminal sample sets, which is the partition needed to regroup the empirical loss after a leafwise update. The supplier is a draft; its body is read, with no approval claimed.

The actual theorem certifies that each CART fit used by the boosting algorithm terminates with a finite tree and nonempty leaves. The consumer proves the loss inequality for each completed round and uses this finite partition. The theorem and relevant supplier proof were inspected; this is not draft acceptance.

The actual Definition fixes the root training-index set and defines its terminal leaf and region semantics. The example uses one root leaf on two observations. The supplier is a draft; its body is read, with no approval claimed.

With maximum depth zero, the actual algorithm leaves the root unsplit and assigns the regression-mean prediction to its sole leaf. For residual targets +1 and -1 that prediction is 0; the example then applies the distinct loss-line minimization specified by its local gradient-boosting algorithm. The supplier is a draft; its body is read, with no approval claimed.
